title: Duchy of Nassau
capsule: The Duchy of Nassau was a German state created in 1806 when Napoleonic reorganization merged the disparate Nassau territories under Duke Frederick Augustus, who joined the Confederation of the Rhine. Straddling the Lahn and Rhine valleys in what are now Hesse and Rhineland-Palatinate, the duchy adopted a relatively liberal constitution in 1814 and developed one of the early German railway networks. Duke Adolf (reigned 1839–1866) pursued an independent foreign policy but backed Austria in the Austro-Prussian War of 1866; Prussia annexed the duchy outright following the Prussian victory by the Treaty of Prague. Adolf later became Grand Duke of Luxembourg in 1890, ensuring the Nassau dynasty's survival despite the duchy's extinction.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Borders of the Duchy of Nassau are well documented through Napoleonic and German Confederation administrative records, though the duchy's fragmented pre-1806 holdings make the earlier period more complex to map.
